world_news.head: ELVES COMPLETE TREE CENSUS, FIND ONE MISSING
world_news.body: Officials at {retreat} have spent eleven years counting every tree in their forest and report one unaccounted for. Suspicion has fallen on a dwarven caravan that passed through carrying, in the words of one elf, 'an extremely suspicious quantity of chairs.' The caravan has declined to comment.

world_news.head: {darkfort} BUILDS TALLER TOWER, OUT OF SPITE
world_news.body: Goblins at {darkfort} have added three storeys to their central tower after learning that {darkfort2} had added two. Engineers warn the structure is now held together mainly by grudges. Residents report that the view from the top is 'mostly other towers.'

world_news.head: HUMAN MAYOR ELECTED ON STRENGTH OF HAT
world_news.body: Voters in {town} have chosen a new mayor after a close campaign decided largely by headwear. The winning hat was described as 'tall and confident.' The losing candidate, who wore no hat at all, has conceded gracefully and is reportedly considering a helmet.

world_news.head: {hillock} RUNS DRY; ENVOYS WEEP
world_news.body: The neighbouring fortress of {hillock} has run out of drink for the first time in living memory. Dwarves there are said to be working at roughly the speed of a sleeping badger. Our own stockpile stands at {drinks}, and the bookkeeper has asked that nobody mention this to them.

world_news.head: NECROMANCER TOWER NEAR {town} TO LET
world_news.body: A tall tower outside {town} has come onto the market after its previous occupant was 'retired' by a passing adventurer. Agents describe it as atmospheric, with quiet neighbours who rarely leave the basement. Buyers are advised to check under the floor for prior tenants.

world_news.head: KOBOLDS HOLD CONVENTION; ALL CHAIRS STOLEN
world_news.body: A gathering of kobold chieftains in the hills of {world} ended abruptly when it was discovered that every chair, table and lectern at the venue had been taken home by the attendees. Organisers have called the event a tremendous success by kobold standards.

world_news.head: ELVES DEMAND APOLOGY FROM A TABLE
world_news.body: Diplomats from {retreat} have formally demanded an apology from a wooden table currently held at our trade depot. The table has not responded. The broker offered to sand it down 'as a gesture,' which the elves described as an atrocity with extra steps.

world_news.head: LOST SNATCHER ASKS GUARDS FOR DIRECTIONS
world_news.body: A goblin snatcher was seen outside the walls of {town} this week politely asking the guards which way the children were. Guards pointed him towards {darkfort2}, which he later described as 'the wrong children.' He is said to be reconsidering his career.

world_news.head: HUMANS MINT NEW COIN, IMMEDIATELY LOSE IT
world_news.body: The mint at {town} unveiled a new gold coin on Tuesday and misplaced it by Wednesday. A search of the market turned up several cats, a goose, and a dwarf who insists he was 'only holding it for safety.' The dwarf is from here. We apologise.

world_news.head: {hillock} DECLARES CATS A NATURAL DISASTER
world_news.body: Overseers at {hillock} have formally reclassified their cat population as a natural disaster after the animals came to outnumber dwarves four to one. Relief barrels of fish have been requested. Our own fortress keeps {cats} cats and wishes to stress that this is entirely normal and fine.

world_news.head: WEREBEAST 'JUST HAVING A ROUGH MONTH'
world_news.body: A resident of {town} who turns into a large hairy beast once a month has asked his neighbours to be more understanding. 'Everyone has their moods,' he said, standing beside a chewed door. The town council has responded by installing more doors.

world_news.head: MAPMAKERS ADMIT THEY MADE UP THE EAST
world_news.body: Scholars in {town} have confessed that the eastern portion of the map of {world} was drawn from memory by a cartographer who had never been there. 'It felt like it should have some mountains,' he explained. Travellers are advised to bring a shovel, just in case.

world_news.head: {darkfort} TRADE FAIR SELLS OUT OF SPEARS
world_news.body: The annual trade fair at {darkfort} closed early after every spear was bought by a single customer, who was also from {darkfort}. Economists describe the goblin economy as 'circular, and pointy.' Next year's theme will once again be 'Sieges: Who, Where, When?'

world_news.head: ELF RECITES 900-VERSE POEM TO ONE OAK
world_news.body: A bard from {retreat} has completed a poem in honour of a single oak tree. The performance lasted nineteen days. The oak was reportedly moved. Our own bards have offered a rebuttal poem about a log, which the elves have described as a threat.

world_news.head: HUMANS DISCOVER PLUMP HELMETS, ARE ALARMED
world_news.body: Food critics in {town2} sampled roasted plump helmets for the first time and described them as 'chewy, purple, and somehow judging us.' The dish has been banned from three taverns and become fashionable in four others. Dwarves continue to eat them without comment.

world_news.head: {hillock} BOOKKEEPER NEVER SLEEPS OR ERRS
world_news.body: Dwarves at {hillock} have raised concerns about their bookkeeper, who has kept flawless records for ninety years, never eats, never sleeps, and is quite pale. Several citizens have died mysteriously in the night. The overseer insists this is 'just what good accountants look like.'

world_news.head: DWARF VISITING {town} SEES SKY, FAINTS
world_news.body: A dwarven merchant on business in {town} looked up by accident on Thursday and has not stopped screaming. Humans, who look at the sky regularly, have been unsympathetic. Physicians recommend a dark room, a strong drink, and replacing the sky with a nice ceiling.

world_news.head: {darkfort2} UNVEILS NEW CAPTIVITY BENEFITS
world_news.body: The demon lords of {darkfort2} have announced a revised package for kidnapped citizens, including weekends off from the pit and a dental plan. Recruitment remains low. A spokesgoblin blamed 'negative press from towns that keep surviving.'

world_news.head: FORGOTTEN BEAST BECOMES TOURIST ATTRACTION
world_news.body: A giant spider made of salt has taken up residence in the caverns below {town} and is drawing record crowds. Ticket sales are strong, although return-ticket sales are very low. The beast has been given a name, a little hat, and a strict no-feeding policy.

world_news.head: HILL TITAN SITS ON {hillock}; ROOF HOLDS
world_news.body: A hill titan wandered into {hillock} this season and sat down on the main entrance for a rest. Engineers there are delighted that the roof held. Residents are less delighted that nobody can get out. Negotiations, conducted through a crack, continue.

world_news.head: FISHERMAN BITTEN, CARP UNREPENTANT
world_news.body: A fisherman in {town} lost a sleeve and most of his confidence to a carp this week. The carp was later seen in the river looking pleased. Dwarven experts note that carp remain the most dangerous thing in {world}, ahead of dragons and paperwork.

world_news.head: SOCK SHORTAGE GRIPS {town2}
world_news.body: Markets in {town2} have run out of socks after a dwarven caravan bought every pair on offer. The caravan leader explained that dwarves 'go through socks the way elves go through feelings.' Humans are now wearing gloves on their feet and complaining loudly.

world_news.head: ELVES RETURN OUR GIFT, CITING 'WOODINESS'
world_news.body: A finely crafted ☼cedar box☼ sent to {retreat} as a token of friendship has been returned with a note reading simply 'how dare you.' Our diplomats are puzzled. Next year we plan to send stone, which the elves are expected to find upsetting for different reasons.

world_news.head: GOBLINS PUBLISH SIEGE CALENDAR AT LAST
world_news.body: Planners at {darkfort} have released a calendar of next year's sieges so that target settlements can 'make arrangements.' {town} is pencilled in for spring. {hillock} is down as 'maybe.' Our fortress is listed under 'if we get round to it,' which the militia commander calls rude.

world_news.head: TAVERN BANS DWARVES, THEN BEGS THEM BACK
world_news.body: A tavern in {town} banned dwarven customers last month after an incident involving a thrown mug and a wall. It reopened this week, having nearly gone out of business without them. The owner now keeps a stack of spare mugs specifically for throwing.

world_news.head: NECROMANCER SEEKS HELP, LIVING PREFERRED
world_news.body: A necromancer in the hills near {town2} has advertised for an apprentice, stating that his current staff 'lack initiative and keep falling apart.' Applicants should be able to read, carry books and tolerate the smell. Dental is not provided, as most staff have no teeth.

world_news.head: SCHOLARS RENAME THE AGE, AGAIN
world_news.body: The scholars of {world} have voted to rename the current era for the fourth time this century. Proposals included 'The Age of Mild Concern' and 'The Bit After the Dragons.' The final choice will be announced once someone remembers which age it currently is.

world_news.head: {hillock} ACCUSES US OF STEALING MIGRANTS
world_news.body: Leaders at {hillock} complain that migrants bound for their fortress keep 'taking a wrong turn' and arriving at {fort} instead. Our overseer denies this, adding that if migrants prefer a place with {pop} dwarves and a functioning well, that is entirely their own business.

world_news.head: {retreat} DECLARES WAR ON A TURNIP
world_news.body: Elves at {retreat} have declared war on a turnip found 'growing in a disrespectful direction.' The turnip has been surrounded. Analysts expect the conflict to last several years, as the elves refuse to harm the turnip and the turnip refuses to move.

world_news.head: GOBLIN POET WINS PRIZE FOR 'SPEAR'
world_news.body: A goblin from {darkfort} has won the annual poetry prize for a work titled 'Spear, Spear, Spear, Also a Fire.' Judges praised its directness. The runner-up, an ode to kidnapping, was criticised as 'a bit soft.' Readings will be held in the dungeon. Attendance is compulsory.

world_news.head: CARAVAN TWO YEARS LATE, GOAT IN CHARGE
world_news.body: A human caravan that set out from {town} in search of our trade depot has finally arrived, having taken what its leader called 'the scenic route, through four wars.' The wagon contained mostly cloth and a goat. The goat is now the caravan leader.

world_news.head: {town2} BUILDS BRIDGE TO NOWHERE ON PURPOSE
world_news.body: Humans in {town2} have completed a bridge over a dry gully, explaining it was 'in case a river turns up.' Dwarven engineers asked why they had not simply connected it to a lever, as is customary. The humans asked what the lever was for. Talks broke down.

world_news.head: BARON DEMANDS JADE PLATES; GUESTS JAILED
world_news.body: The baron of {town} hosted a feast for four hundred guests and demanded that every plate be made of jade. None of the guests owned jade plates. Several were imprisoned. Our own nobles have taken careful notes and are said to be 'very inspired.'

world_news.head: {hillock} HITS AQUIFER, IS NOW A LAKE
world_news.body: Miners at {hillock} struck an aquifer on the third level and the fortress is now, technically, a lake. Residents report that the fishing is excellent but the beds are wet. A spokesdwarf said morale is 'high, mostly because we are floating.'

world_news.head: NEW LIBRARY LENDS ONLY BOOK; NEVER RETURNED
world_news.body: The new library in {town} opened its doors and lent its single book to a visiting dwarven scholar, who has since left town. The library would like the book back. Our own library wishes to state, for the record, that it has a new book.

world_news.head: ELVES AND GOBLINS SIGN PACT; DEER EATS IT
world_news.body: Envoys from {retreat} and {darkfort} have signed a treaty of mutual friendship, written in elvish on a leaf. The goblins cannot read elvish and the leaf has since been eaten by a deer. Both sides are at war again, which observers describe as restful.

world_news.head: IT IS ALSO {weather} IN {town}, HUMANS SAY
world_news.body: Correspondents report that the weather in {town} this {season} is broadly the same as ours, which humans find fascinating and dwarves find irrelevant, as we live inside a mountain. One human asked what the weather was like underground. We said 'rock.'

world_news.head: DRAGON RETIRES, OPENS BAKERY
world_news.body: A dragon that terrorised the country around {town2} for three centuries has retired and opened a bakery. Reviews praise the even crust. Regulars report that complaints are dealt with 'promptly, and with fire.' Nobody has yet left a tip, and nobody has yet survived not leaving one.

world_news.head: HUMAN STUDY FINDS DWARVES 'SHORTER'
world_news.body: Scholars in {town} have published a lengthy study concluding that dwarves are, on average, shorter than humans. Dwarven academics responded with a counter-study concluding that humans are 'mostly legs, and needlessly so.' Both studies were funded by the same tavern.

world_news.head: GOBLIN AMBUSH TURNED BACK BY A BABY
world_news.body: A goblin ambush near {hillock} was repelled by a dwarven mother carrying her infant into battle, as is tradition. The baby bit a goblin captain on the ear. {darkfort} has filed a complaint about 'unsporting use of children,' which is rich, coming from them.

world_news.head: ELVES OFFER TO TRADE A BEAR FOR A HUG
world_news.body: The latest elven caravan from {retreat} arrived with a single tame bear and an offer to swap it for 'emotional sincerity.' Our broker offered a crate of ☼iron bolts☼ instead. Negotiations ended in tears on both sides, though the bear seemed fine.

world_news.head: {town2} TAXES ANYONE WITH A BEARD
world_news.body: Authorities in {town2} have introduced a beard tax at the city gate. One dwarven merchant paid in full and then refused to leave, saying he had 'paid for the gate and intended to use it.' He has been living in the gatehouse since spring and is now on the council.

world_news.head: WORLD NOT ENDING AFTER ALL, SAYS PROPHET
world_news.body: A prophet from {town} has announced that {world} will not end this year after all, having miscounted. Earlier predictions coincided with goblin sieges, which he admits 'felt very end-of-the-world at the time.' He is now predicting a mild {season}.

world_news.head: MOODY CRAFTSDWARF ABROAD WANTS OUR BONES
world_news.body: A craftsdwarf at {hillock} has been seized by a strange mood and is demanding shells, bones and 'whatever {fort} has.' Envoys arrived this week asking to borrow some. Our overseer has lent a pile of goblin bones, which the envoys said were 'hardly used.'

travel.head: A WEEKEND IN {darkfort}: ONE STAR
travel.body: The welcome was warm, mainly because the reception hall was on fire. Our room had no bed, no window, and a goblin who stood in the corner all night 'for security.' Breakfast was a spear. Would not return, though the goblins insist we will.

travel.head: {retreat}: LOVELY TREES, NO CHAIRS
travel.body: The elves of {retreat} are charming hosts, provided you never sit down, never eat anything cooked, and never mention axes. We spent four days standing politely. The food was berries. The entertainment was a tree. Our reviewer has recommended it to his enemies.

travel.head: {town}: SO MUCH SKY
travel.body: The humans of {town} build their houses above ground, under the open sky, deliberately. Our correspondent spent the trip hiding under a cart. Shops were adequate, beer was thin, and every single street had weather on it. Two stars, both for the cart.

travel.head: {hillock}: LIKE HOME, BUT WORSE
travel.body: A short walk from {fort} and a long way below our standards. The dining hall has no tables, the well has no water, and the famous engraver is just a dwarf who scratched 'URIST WAS HERE' on everything. Good beer, though. Three stars.

travel.head: CAVERNS UNDER {town2}: BRING A SWORD
travel.body: Visitors can enjoy glowing mushrooms, quiet lakes, and the forgotten beast living in the quiet lake. Our guide was very knowledgeable until about halfway through. The gift shop is excellent. Recommended only to those who have already written their wills.

travel.head: RIVER CRUISE FROM {town}: AVOID
travel.body: The brochure promised 'a gentle drift past fields and willows.' It did not mention the carp. Our party of six returned as a party of four and a sleeve. The captain apologised and offered us a discount, which the carp also took.

travel.head: {darkfort2}: TRULY ALL-INCLUSIVE
travel.body: Everything is included at {darkfort2}, whether you asked for it or not: food, lodging, chains, and a lifelong job. Check-out is famously difficult. Staff are attentive to the point of never letting you out of their sight. Not suitable for children, though the staff disagree.

travel.head: CAMPING IN THE WILDS OF {world}
travel.body: Our reviewer slept under the stars for the first time and found it deeply upsetting. The ground was the wrong shape, the stars kept moving, and a bear ate his hat. He has since dug a hole in the bathroom and refuses to come out of it.

travel.head: {town2} MARKET DAY: OVERPRICED
travel.body: Humans at {town2} charge eight silver for a single loaf of bread, then look surprised when you offer them a rock. The rock was ☼granite☼. They did not appreciate it. We came home with nothing but a pigeon, which followed us.

travel.head: {retreat} SPA: SEVERAL HUGS
travel.body: The elven spa offers mud baths, forest bathing and 'tree listening.' Our reviewer listened to a tree for three hours and reports that it said nothing. When he asked whether the tree might make a nice cabinet, the session ended abruptly. No refunds.

travel.head: A NIGHT AT THE NECROMANCER'S TOWER
travel.body: Just outside {town}, this boutique tower offers stunning views and a large, quiet staff. Room service was slow but persistent. Our reviewer woke to find a skeleton tucking him in. Friendly, if bony. Four stars, minus one for the moaning.

travel.head: {hillock} TAVERN: LIVELY
travel.body: The tavern at {hillock} has a resident bard who knows one song. He sang it eleven times. On the twelfth, a dwarf threw a mug, and the evening really got going. Best night out in years, according to the dwarf, who is still in the hospital.

travel.head: SIGHTSEEING TOUR OF {darkfort}
travel.body: Highlights include the Big Tower, the Slightly Smaller Tower, and the Pit. Our guide encouraged us to 'get a closer look' at the Pit. We declined. The guide was disappointed. Lunch was not provided, as several of us were briefly considered as lunch.

travel.head: {town} CASTLE: GREAT WALLS, POOR DOORS
travel.body: The castle at {town} has excellent walls, which our engineer reviewer spent two days admiring, and very poor doors, which he spent two days criticising. He never saw the inside, as the guards objected to him tapping everything with a hammer.

travel.head: SKIING ABOVE {hillock}
travel.body: Dwarves do not ski. Our reviewer tried it anyway and discovered why. He now lives at the bottom of the mountain, roughly where the snow put him, and runs a small but successful bar out of the drift. Recommended, in a way.

travel.head: {retreat} DINING: A LEAF ON A LEAF
travel.body: Elven restaurants cook without fire, carve without knives and serve without plates. Dinner was a leaf on a leaf. Dessert was the second leaf. Our reviewer brought his own roasted plump helmet and was asked to leave by a very upset moose.

travel.head: THE ROAD TO {town2}: SCENIC
travel.body: Six days of glorious hills, babbling streams and almost no sieges. Our reviewer was robbed only twice, both times by the same bandit, who seemed to recognise him. Inns along the way serve thin beer and thick soup. It should be the other way round.

travel.head: PILGRIMAGE TO THE EDGE OF {world}
travel.body: Legend holds that the edge of the world is a cliff, a sea or a wall. Our reviewer walked for three months and found more of the same scrubland. Disappointing. He has proposed building a wall there, to make the trip worthwhile.

travel.head: {darkfort} BY NIGHT: MOSTLY SCREAMING
travel.body: Nightlife at {darkfort} centres on the dungeons, which stay open late. There is a lively music scene, if you count drums and screaming. The food court sells roasted something. Our reviewer did not ask what, and has since become a vegetarian, which the elves have praised.

travel.head: HONEYMOON IN {town}
travel.body: Newlyweds spent a romantic week in {town}, enjoying candlelit dinners, walks by the river, and a brief imprisonment for 'excessive axe.' They describe the trip as perfect and the cell as 'well constructed, honestly. Lovely masonry.'

travel.head: {hillock} HOT SPRINGS: TOO HOT
travel.body: The hot springs at {hillock} turned out to be the magma sea, which had been poorly signposted. Our reviewer survived thanks to his iron boots and a rapid sense of direction. He rates the springs 'too hot' and the signposting 'lethal.'

travel.head: A GUIDED HIKE THROUGH {retreat}
travel.body: The elves offer walks through their ancient forest, provided you remove your boots, your axe and your opinions. Our reviewer kept his opinions. They were about lumber. He has been banned from the forest and, separately, from three nearby hedges.

travel.head: {town2} THEATRE: WE DIDN'T GET IT
travel.body: The humans of {town2} staged a three-hour play about a king who is sad. Nobody threw anything. Nobody fought a beast. Nobody even drank. Our reviewer clapped politely at the end and went to find a tavern with a proper fight in it.

travel.head: CARAVAN HOLIDAY: {town} TO {fort}
travel.body: Why not travel in the back of a trade wagon, between a crate of leather and a crate of more leather? Highlights: the depot, a goat, and an elf who would not stop talking. Lowlights: everything else, and the ambush. Five stars from the goat.

travel.head: {darkfort2} SUMMER CAMP
travel.body: Children are welcome at {darkfort2} all year round and are, in fact, actively collected. Activities include spear practice, tower climbing and joining the goblin army. Parents are not invited. Parents, we are told, are 'not needed.' Strongly not recommended.

travel.head: MINING HOLIDAY UNDER {town}
travel.body: Humans have dug a modest mine under {town} and invite visitors to 'try their hand.' Our reviewer struck the earth, then struck it some more, and was halfway to {hillock} before anyone noticed. The humans now have a very long tunnel and a lawyer.

travel.head: A WEEK AMONG THE KOBOLDS OF {world}
travel.body: Kobold hospitality is famously informal. You arrive with a backpack, a sword and a purse. You leave with a story. The kobolds keep everything else. Our reviewer says they were 'lovely, really' and is still looking for his left boot.

letters_abroad.body: I write from {town}, where the humans eat their dinner on top of the ground like animals. I have asked for a table in the cellar and been refused. Please send soap, socks and a small amount of ceiling.
May I protest, through your pages, the treatment of a table I sold to the elves of {retreat}? They have given it a funeral. It was a perfectly good table. It had years left in it.

I have been held captive at {darkfort} for six years and must complain that the Herald has not been delivered once. The goblins say there is 'no post' here. Kindly correct this at your earliest convenience.
letters_abroad.by: A Subscriber, in a Cage at {darkfort}

letters_abroad.body: Having visited {hillock}, I can confirm their beer is weaker than ours, their beards shorter and their well a disgrace. I enclose a sample of their stone for your readers to laugh at.
Would the dwarf who left a crate of plump helmets on my doorstep in {town2} kindly come and collect it? It has begun to sprout, and the children are frightened of it.
I am a goblin and I wish to say that not all goblins enjoy sieges. Some of us would prefer to stay home and knit. I knit spears, mainly, but the point stands.
The elves here keep asking how I 'feel about the forest.' I feel it would make a lovely set of beds. This answer has not been popular. I may be home sooner than planned.
Is it true that {fort} has {pop} dwarves and only one well? We at {hillock} have three wells and nobody left to drink from them. Would you swap some dwarves for a well?
I travelled to the far edge of the world at great expense and found a small rock. I have brought it back. It is not a very good rock. I just wanted somebody to know.
Whilst visiting {town}, I attended a human wedding at which nobody brawled, nobody wept and nobody threw a single mug. Are humans well? Should someone check on them?
The humans of {town2} keep cats as pets, not as an unstoppable force of nature. They have three. Three cats! I asked their secret. They said 'shutting the door.' I do not understand.
The humans here asked me what a 'danger room' is. I explained it, with diagrams. They have called the guard. Please send a lawyer, or at least a strongly worded engraving.
I have lived among the kobolds for a year as part of a scholarly study. They have taken my notes, my quill, my boots and my name. I am now called 'Shiny.' I am happy.
May I recommend {town2} to any dwarf seeking a quiet holiday? There are no aquifers, no forgotten beasts and no nobles. I have never been so bored in my life. I return on Tuesday.
The goblins of {darkfort} have a newspaper of their own. It is called 'Spear.' Every page reads 'SPEAR.' I find it refreshing, compared with certain other papers.
Why does the caravan from {town} always arrive just as the goblins do? I am not saying the humans are leading the goblins here. I am simply noting it, in ink, publicly.
I was sent by the King to inspect the outposts of {world}. Yours has a moat filled with magma and a sign that says 'WELCOME.' Which of these is the true message?
The elves have asked me to tell your readers that the trees are watching. I have checked. They are. I have stopped writing near trees. I am writing this one in a hole.
My cousin at {hillock} says their militia trains for nine hours a day. Ours trains for two, then has a drink. I know which fortress I would rather live in, and it is not theirs.
I am a vampire, and would like to clarify that I am also a very good bookkeeper. If your fortress has any openings, I promise never to bite the overseer. Much.
I sailed home on a human boat. It floated on top of the water, all day, in plain view of the carp. Never again. I will walk the rest. It will take a year. Worth it.
letters_abroad.by: A Dwarf Who Has Seen Things

letters_abroad.body: Kindly inform my former neighbours that I have opened a tavern abroad, and that I still have all the mugs they threw at me. They are for sale, as souvenirs.
Please send word to my wife that I am safe and have not been eaten by anything. Please do not send word to my wife about the tavern, the dice, or the goat.
I would like an apology for being called 'a hill' in your last issue. I am a titan. The hill is something I stand on. I am coming to visit, to discuss it.
Having toured {darkfort}, {darkfort2} and several smaller goblin towers, I can confirm they are all the same tower. Same architect. Same spikes. Not one engraving of a cheese.
The elves have offered me citizenship if I renounce stone. I counter-offered that I would renounce trees. They seemed to think this was the same thing. It is not.
Could whoever keeps sending migrants from {town} please include a note saying what they are good at? The last seven were all fish dissectors. We do not have that many fish.

lines: FROM THE SAFETY OF A CART
Cart has a roof. Roof has a smaller roof. Sky visible only by appointment.
Survives spears, fire and snatchers. Contents not guaranteed. Owner very much not guaranteed.
400 ways to say 'nice tree' and none of the words for 'chair.' Printed on stone. Do not take to {retreat}.
Price includes wagon, goat, guards and ambush. Ambush cannot be cancelled. Neither can the goat.
Rooms carved from solid rock. Some rock still in the rooms. Breakfast is plump helmet. So is lunch.
For dwarves visiting {town} and other places with too much up. Fits under one arm. Does not fold.
Keep hands, beards and opinions inside the boat at all times. The carp are listening.
*Ransom paid in socks. Goblins have never once accepted socks. Policy void if you were already a goblin.
Portable barrels for dwarves visiting {town}, where the beer is thin and the barmen thinner. Holds a weekend.
One-hour course: bowing, smiling, not calling anything 'kindling.' Recommended before any visit to {retreat}.
Tour leaves the gate in spring. Returning party size not guaranteed. Souvenir rock included.
Learn to say 'where is the cellar' and 'please stop showing me the sky' in the tongue of {town2}.
Goblins also hate us, you, your fortress and mornings generally. Results may vary near {darkfort2}.
Voted second-best fortress within walking distance of {fort}, in a poll of one dwarf from {hillock}.
Also cloth, a goat and a very confused elf. Prices marked in ☼ quality. Haggling encouraged, mugs discouraged.
For travellers who did not survive {darkfort}. Ghost-proof lid. Family discounts available, unfortunately.
Staff are skeletal but enthusiastic. Please do not take bones as souvenirs. They belong to the guide.
Made for dwarves passing the gates of {town2}. Fits beards up to four feet. Longer beards, see manager.
Eastern regions drawn from memory. Mountains added for flavour. Please return this map if you find the east.
Humans may find them chewy and alarming. That is their problem. Purple guaranteed, freshness not.
Woven at {retreat} from living vines. The vines remain alive. The vines have opinions about you.
Know exactly when the goblins are coming so you can be elsewhere, say {town}. Dates subject to goblin whim.
